scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Every app, game and video on your phone runs on a chip smaller than a fingernail. How does a processor actually think?

scenes.name: transistors
scenes.text: A processor is made of billions of transistors, tiny switches that are either on or off, one or zero.

scenes.name: gates
scenes.text: Transistors are wired into logic gates, which combine ones and zeros to add numbers and make decisions.

scenes.name: cycle
scenes.text: The CPU repeats a cycle. Fetch an instruction from memory, decode what it means, then execute it.

scenes.name: clock
scenes.text: A clock ticks billions of times a second, measured in gigahertz, keeping every step in sync.

scenes.name: cores
scenes.text: Modern chips have several cores, each like a separate processor, so many tasks run at the same time.

scenes.name: cache
scenes.text: A small, super fast memory called cache sits on the chip, so the CPU doesn't wait for slower memory.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Switches, gates, a ticking clock. Billions of simple steps. Follow for more on how things really work.
